issues.legal_issue: A private complaint cannot initiate prosecution for abetting the fabrication of a false court record intended to be used in a judicial proceeding to create an erroneous opinion on a material point.
material_facts: A public servant was alleged to have made a false entry about a case pending in court, intending that the entry be used in the proceeding to create an erroneous opinion about when it was instituted.
The private complainant charged another person with abetting the public servant’s act and filed no complaint from the court concerned.
issues.conclusion: The prosecution for abetment could not proceed on the private complaint; it required a written complaint from the court concerned.
issues.legal_principle: Fabricating false evidence within IPC Section 192 includes making a false entry intended to appear in evidence in a judicial proceeding and cause an erroneous opinion on a material point. The offence is punishable under IPC Section 193, and CrPC Section 195(1)(b) bars cognizance of it, including its abetment, unless the court concerned makes a written complaint. IPC Section 218 does not govern an entry made for that judicial-evidence purpose rather than to save or injure a person or property.

rule.if: private_complaint_without_court_complaint and prosecution_for_abetting_record_maker and false_record_for_judicial_use and intended_material_judicial_error

predicates.private_complaint_without_court_complain: A private complainant initiated prosecution without a written complaint from the court concerned.
predicates.prosecution_for_abetting_record_maker: The prosecution alleged that a person abetted the maker of a record.
predicates.false_record_for_judicial_use: The record maker allegedly made a false record intending that it be used as evidence in a judicial proceeding.
predicates.intended_material_judicial_error: The record maker allegedly intended the false record to cause an erroneous opinion on a material point in the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a private complainant prosecutes alleged abetment of making a false record for judicial use to cause a material error, and the court concerned has not made a written complaint, a court complaint is required.

issues.legal_issue: A private complaint may proceed for abetting a public servant’s intentional preparation of a false record to save or injure a person or property when the offence does not depend on use of the record in a judicial proceeding.
material_facts: Public servants were alleged to have caused an incorrect land record to be prepared, knowing it was likely to cause loss or injury to the purchasers of the land.
The alleged purpose was to save the property from the effects of the sale, and the offence did not require the record to be used in a judicial proceeding.
The private complainant charged another person with abetting the public servants’ acts.
issues.conclusion: The private complaint could proceed against the alleged abettor; the bar on cognizance without a court complaint did not apply.
issues.legal_principle: IPC Section 218 creates a distinct offence involving a public servant’s intentional preparation of a false record to save or injure a person or property; it is complete when the record is made with that intention and does not require judicial use of the record. It is not a minor offence included within IPC Section 192 and is not among the offences covered by CrPC Section 195. Accordingly, that section does not bar a private complaint alleging the offence or its abetment.

rule.if: private_complaint_without_court_complaint and prosecution_for_abetting_record_maker and public_servant_made_false_record and intended_to_save_or_injure_person_or_property and not intended_material_judicial_error

predicates.private_complaint_without_court_complain: A private complainant initiated prosecution without a written complaint from the court concerned.
predicates.prosecution_for_abetting_record_maker: The prosecution alleged that a person abetted the maker of a record.
predicates.public_servant_made_false_record: A public servant allegedly intentionally prepared a false record.
predicates.intended_to_save_or_injure_person_or_pro: The public servant allegedly prepared the record to save or injure a person or property.
predicates.intended_material_judicial_error: The record maker allegedly intended the false record to cause an erroneous opinion on a material point in a judicial proceeding.

issues.definition: When a private complainant alleges abetment of a public servant’s intentional false record made to save or injure a person or property, rather than to cause a material judicial error, the private complaint can proceed.
